Rashi on Yevamot 8b:1:1.hebrew: למישרי צרה שלא במקום מצוה - דאי לא כתיב עליה, הוה ילפינן מלצרור דצרת אחות אשה אסורה בכל מקום:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:1:1.english: To permit a rival wife in a place where the mitzva is not applicable - For had “with her” not been written, we would have derived from “to be a rival” that the rival wife of a wife's sister is forbidden in all circumstances.

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:1:2.hebrew: מאי טעמא - כלומר, היכי מידרשא היתר מהכא:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:1:2.english: What is the reason - That is to say: How is permission derived from here?

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:1:3.hebrew: במקום עליה הוא - דכתיב לצרור למיסר צרה, ולא במקום אחר:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:1:3.english: It is in a place of “with her” - For it is written “to be a rival wife” to prohibit a rival wife, and not in another place.

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:2:1.hebrew: אימא ערוה גופה שלא במקום מצוה תשתרי - מדכתיב עליה, דקאי נמי אאחות אשה:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:2:1.english: Say that the forbidden relative herself, [when] not in a place of a mitzvah, should be permitted - Since it is written “upon her,” which also applies to a wife’s sister.

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:3:1.english: As long as [she is] in her lifetime - [Throughout the lifetime of] your wife, you shall not marry her sister.

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:6:1.hebrew: תרי קראי כתיבי - מעיקרא כתיב ״לצרור״, דמשמע לא היא ולא צרתה; והדר כתיב ״לגלות ערותה״, דמשמע חדא הוא דאסירא:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:6:1.english: Two verses are written - Initially, it is written 'to be a rival,' which implies that neither she nor her rival wife [is permitted]; and then it is written 'to uncover her nakedness,' which implies that only one [of them] is forbidden.

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:6:2.hebrew: במקום מצוה שתיהן אסורין - כדכתיב ״עליה״, דמשמע: במקום ״עליה״:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:6:2.english: In a place of [a] mitzva, both of them are prohibited - As it is written: “Upon her” [Leviticus 18:18], which implies: in the place of “upon her” [i.e., where the mitzva of levirate marriage applies, as it is written: “Her brother-in-law will have intercourse with her” (Deuteronomy 25:5)].

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:7:1.hebrew: ואיפוך אנא במקום מצוה היא אסורה וצרתה מותרת - דהא עליה אלגלות ערותה סמיך, דמשמע חדא, למדרש הכי: במקו' עליה הוא דלא אסיר לן אלא חדא, וקרא דלצרור — אשלא במקום מצוה:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:7:1.english: And I can reverse [this]: In a place of a mitzvah, she is forbidden and her rival wife is permitted - For behold, “upon her” is adjacent to “to uncover her nakedness,” which implies one [woman], to expound [it] thus: In the place of “upon her” [i.e., levirate marriage], it is that [the Torah] prohibited only one [woman] to us; and the verse’s [phrase] “to be rivals” [applies] to where there is no mitzvah.

Rashi on Yevamot 8b:7:2.hebrew: א"כ לא יאמר עליה - דבלא עליה נמי, כי קשו לן קראי אהדדי, משנינן להו מסברא הכי: היתירא למצוה, ואיסורא שלא במקום מצוה. הלכך, עליה לחדושי אתא — למדרשיה אלצרור, ולמיסר צרה במקום מצוה כערוה:
Rashi on Yevamot 8b:7:2.english: If so, let [the verse] not say “upon her” - For even without “upon her,” when the verses contradicted each other, we would resolve them by reasoning thus: the permission [applies] to [a place of] the mitzvah, and the prohibition [applies] where there is no mitzvah. Therefore, “upon her” came to innovate — to expound it in connection with “to be a rival” [litzror], and to prohibit the rival wife in a place of the mitzvah just like the forbidden relation.

Tosafot on Yevamot 8b:1:1.hebrew: למישרי צרה שלא במקום מצוה - וא"ת: להנהו שינויי דלעיל, דמצרכי קרא לערוה גופה — מנא להו למישרי צרה שלא במקום מצוה? וי"ל: דנפקא להו מהיכא דנפקא ליה לרבי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 8b:1:1.english: "To permit a rival wife in a place where the mitzva is not applicable" - And if you say: According to those resolutions above that require a verse for the forbidden relation herself, from where do they derive to permit a rival wife in a place where the mitzva is not applicable? And it can be answered that they derive it from where Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] derives it.
